results.title: Effectuation in action: how pre-commitments drive international ...
results.content: This study examines small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) entrepreneurial internationalization by exploring how effectual decision-making principles and real options reasoning (specifically pre-commitment, staging logic, and affordable loss (influence the creation of foreign market entry opportunities and international performance in 332 New Zealand SMEs. It demonstrates that pre-commitment not only initiates but also drives opportunity creation, which in turn enhances international performance. Effectuation principles, including affordable loss and pre-commitment, balance exploration, and risk management, support opportunity creation, while staging logic reinforces this process by enabling continuous assessment and adaptation (Buccieri et al., 2023. Affordable loss and staging logic mediate the effect of pre-commitment on FME opportunity creation, while experiential learning moderates the link between opportunity creation and international performance. To test the hypothesized mediation effects and the direct relationships among pre-commitment, foreign market entry opportunity creation, and international performance, we followed Gaskin et al. Our findings demonstrate that combining pre-commitment, affordable loss, and staging logic allows SMEs to balance risk and flexibility, enhancing foreign market entry opportunities and international performance.

results.title: The impact of effectuation on international diversity and performance ...
results.content: Using cross-country data from China and Poland, the analysis shows that non-predictive strategy is positively associated with international diversity and the use of affordable loss, and that affordable loss mediates the positive effect of non-predictive strategy on the international performance of SMEs. These findings advance understanding of effectuation in the context of SME internationalization and clarify the distinct roles of non-predictive strategy and affordable loss. Recent research on small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) internationalization has integrated effectuation theory with the traditional internationalization process model to explain how firms expand into foreign markets (Chetty et al., 2024, Sarasvathy et al., 2014). In particular, few studies investigate effectuation in the context of international diversification (Deligianni, 2023), which involves doing business in multiple markets where there is high uncertainty, lack of reliable information and difficulty in predicting the future (Bai et al., 2021, Chetty et al., 2015, Wu et al., 2021).

results.title: From Effectuation to Empowerment: Unveiling the Impact of Women ...
results.content: Drawing on the resource-based view and entrepreneurship effectuation theory, this study examines how women’s entrepreneurial effectuation (WEE) modeled as a higher-order construct (HOC) comprising its four dimensions (LOCs)—namely, flexibility, experimentation, affordable loss, and pre-commitment—can influence employee performance (EMPRF) mediated by structural (STREM) and psychological empowerment (PSYEM). This study seeks to address the following research question: How does effectuation, conceptualized as a multidimensional construct, influence employee performance in women-led SMEs in Indonesia, and to what extent are these effects mediated by structural and psychological empowerment and moderated by gender equality and market orientation? However, the RBV was still limited in its implementation, specifically in how women entrepreneurs can develop and utilize human resources dynamically and adaptively in facing business challenges with limited resources and in the context of emerging countries/SMEs. To that end, this research integrates the RBV with the effectuation approach and empowerment theory to provide a more holistic perspective on SMEs. Specifically, the RBV serves as the theoretical foundation in this study by positioning each variable as a key internal or relational resource contributing to competitive advantage in women-led SMEs. Entrepreneurial effectuation reflects the dynamic ability to flexibly mobilize and reconfigure limited resources (Barney, 1991; Teoh et al., 2021).
